title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE METER MONSTER
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Ray Hutchins, a parking officer in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
One morning, he found out the whole street had a nickname for him.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE NICKNAME
segments.quote: Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if thou wilt ever dig.
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: His niece showed him a photo online. Ray, mid-ticket. The Meter Monster strikes again.
That night he opened his late dad's copy of Marcus Aurelius, the Roman emperor:
Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if thou wilt ever dig.
He'd keep writing tickets. But he'd start digging.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE BAKERY
segments.quote: You never really understand a person until you consider things from his point of view.
segments.author: Harper Lee
lines: Every morning Rosa yelled at him from her bakery door, and every morning her van got a ticket.
Then he remembered Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird:
You never really understand a person until you consider things from his point of view.
So he stood where Rosa stood. Forty trays of bread, nowhere to unload, two bad knees.
He carried the trays. She still yelled, but nicer.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE RED CAR
segments.quote: When dealing with people, remember you are not dealing with creatures of logic, but with creatures of emotion.
segments.author: Dale Carnegie
lines: Then a man ran out to his red sports car, shouting so loud the pigeons left town.
Ray wanted to shout back. Instead he remembered Dale Carnegie:
When dealing with people, remember you are not dealing with creatures of logic, but with creatures of emotion.
So Ray asked what was wrong. A daughter's recital, and a dead battery.
Ray gave him a jump start. And a ticket.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE MEETING
segments.quote: Your most unhappy customers are your greatest source of learning.
segments.author: Bill Gates
lines: Next came a neighborhood meeting about parking. Ray went. In uniform. Brave or foolish, nobody could tell.
For an hour, people complained. Ray took notes, thinking of Bill Gates:
Your most unhappy customers are your greatest source of learning.
Every complaint was the same. Nowhere to unload. Ray stood up and said, You're right.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: CITY HALL
segments.quote: Determine that the thing can and shall be done, and then we shall find the way.
segments.author: Abraham Lincoln
lines: He asked the city for a loading zone. They gave him a form. Then a form about the form.
Six weeks in, he nearly quit. Then he passed a poster of Abraham Lincoln:
Determine that the thing can and shall be done, and then we shall find the way.
Rosa and nine shop owners signed his letter. The sign went up in May.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE PARADE
segments.quote: Rudeness is the weak man's imitation of strength.
segments.author: Eric Hoffer
lines: In December, the same page voted Ray grand marshal of the holiday parade. One man still yelled, Hey, Meter Monster!
Ray remembered Eric Hoffer, the dock worker turned writer:
Rudeness is the weak man's imitation of strength.
Ray just smiled and called back, Happy holidays! Your meter runs out at noon! The whole street laughed. Even the man.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Dig deep. See their side. Mind the feelings. Learn from complaints. Find the way. Smile back.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Dig deep. See their side. Mind the feelings. Learn from complaints. Find the way. Smile back.
Me? I once got a parking ticket in my own driveway. Still digging.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
